about: Source data for the Domino Map. Edit this file, then run: python3 atlas/tools/domino_map.py. It regenerates atlas/domino-map/Domino-Map.md and the interactive map. Nodes are dominoes: current events, character dominoes, and ripple-chain steps. scale 'ground' = a Sunday Morning story can live here; 'saga' = belongs to the main saga, which Sunday Morning stories only feel from the ground. Edge basis: 'canon' = stated on a wiki owner page; 'story' = set by the Sunday Morning collection design (provisional).

nodes.label: Piracy rises
nodes.text: Raids are increasing along the coast. Ripple chain step 1: shipping risk rises.

nodes.label: Convoy patrols and trusted-cove lists
nodes.text: Defensive convoy politics. What looks defensive to Northwind can look like maritime militarization to Sunplains or Port merchants.

nodes.label: Maris Bleakshore
nodes.text: Respected coastal leader shaped by piracy and loss. Pushed with credible but selectively framed intelligence, so defensive action looks necessary.

nodes.label: Fish stocks shift
nodes.text: Some fisheries are declining or moving: price rises, clan disputes, illegal fishing, pressure for new agreements.

nodes.label: Shipping losses; credit and insurance tighten
nodes.text: Merchant conflict: losses, insurance disputes, warehouse fires. Ripple chain step 2: Port insurance and credit tighten.

nodes.label: Smuggling surge
nodes.text: Higher prices and disrupted routes raise demand for illegal transport.

nodes.label: Displaced families arrive
nodes.text: People displaced by border and economic crises arrive faster than housing and charity can absorb them.

nodes.label: Rosana Meadowcroft
nodes.text: Seed steward working on crop resilience. Pushed by funding her research, creating distribution bottlenecks and letting rivals overreact.

nodes.label: Bumper harvest won't sell
nodes.text: A new strain and good weather bring huge yields; prices fall, storage fills, merchants delay, rumors say the grain is unsafe. Ripple chain steps 3 and 4.

nodes.label: Farmers default
nodes.text: Ripple chain step 5: poorer farmers can't cover their debts.

nodes.label: Consolidators buy distressed farms
nodes.text: Large interests acquire failing farms; an agricultural innovation becomes a political fight over control. Ripple chain step 7.

nodes.label: Reformers call it coordinated theft
nodes.text: Ripple chain step 8: religious and guild reformers accuse the buyers of engineering the crisis.

nodes.label: Orin Slatehallow
nodes.text: Talented young metalworker. Pushed with anonymous funding and selective obstruction until he depends on a benefactor.

nodes.label: Good metal vanishing into private contracts
nodes.text: High-quality metal is being redirected. Observers blame smuggling, war preparation, corrupt guild masters or foreign buyers.

nodes.label: Tool orders fall; workshops cut hours
nodes.text: Ripple chain steps 9 and 10: protests hit tool orders from Ironcrest, and workshops reduce hours.

nodes.label: Labor unrest; strike talk
nodes.text: Workers organize around wages, safety, debt and guild control. Ripple chain step 11: strike leaders blame owners.

nodes.label: Caravan attacks
nodes.text: Attacks and disappearances make some routes seem unreliable.

nodes.label: Samir Tareh
nodes.text: Caravan negotiator seeking fair, predictable routes. Given true information about dangers, but not who created them.

nodes.label: Trade concentrates on 'safe' routes
nodes.text: Trade is redirected; bypassed towns suffer at once, and the concentrated route becomes strategically vulnerable.

nodes.label: Debates tied to patrons
nodes.text: Highridge intellectual disputes are increasingly tied to real patrons and commercial interests.

nodes.label: Road and logging plans
nodes.text: New extraction or infrastructure proposals cross disputed local boundaries; some are legal under old treaties.

nodes.label: Naruin Mossglade
nodes.text: Forest warden defending local rights. Pushed by leaking real Council-backed plans without context.

nodes.label: Plans leak; wardens ready to block
nodes.text: Preemptive defense: a local conservation dispute on its way to becoming an inter-regional sovereignty crisis.

nodes.label: Fungal blight on forest foods
nodes.text: A disease or ecological change hits important forest foods; natural, accidental or exploited.

nodes.label: Drought anxiety
nodes.text: Water isn't scarce everywhere yet, but fear drives hoarding, canal guards, secret agreements and speculation.

nodes.label: Bahriyya Nazar
nodes.text: Reformist diplomat coordinating city-states around water and trade. Her coordination is secretly helped, then made to look expansionist.

nodes.label: City-states coordinate
nodes.text: Some leaders try to cooperate; rivals read it as the start of a dominant bloc that justifies counter-alliances.

nodes.label: Spine earthquake
nodes.text: Land movement damages roads and exposes ruins, caves and sealed routes: resource rushes, religious claims, territorial disputes.

nodes.label: Underpass route wars
nodes.text: Collapse and discovery change which enclaves control profitable corridors; smuggling and legitimate trade compete for the same space.

nodes.label: Council steadies the lenders
nodes.text: Ripple chain step 6: Council finance tries to stabilize lenders. Its countermeasures often solve one problem while creating another.

nodes.label: Faiths compare notes
nodes.text: Faiths begin to read the crises across regions: scholars compare records, Weavers document damage, Compass pilgrims carry rumors.

nodes.label: Villain amplifies 'Council involvement'
nodes.text: Ripple chain step 12: Villain agents amplify evidence of Council involvement.

nodes.label: Local shocks read as proof of enemies
nodes.text: Ripple chain step 13: a local economic shock becomes proof, in several regions, that another group is acting against them. The road to mobilization and near-war.

stories.title: One Square, Two Harvests
stories.holds: The Vale eats its 'unsafe' grain in public; no farm sells to the land agent.
stories.elsewhere: Farms elsewhere in Greenvale do sell.

stories.title: The Greenvale Man
stories.holds: Nobody actually saw Narrow Sound shelter raiders; the coves race anyway.
stories.elsewhere: Other coves leave Narrow Sound out of their convoy.

stories.title: The Goat File
stories.holds: Seven Wells clears its books without ruin; two houses will join.
stories.elsewhere: Forced closures ruin families in other towns.

stories.title: Inspected, Not Guaranteed
stories.holds: Col never answers the anonymous patron.

stories.title: The Heavy Scale at Icestep Summit
stories.holds: Icestep corrects its scale in public and stays on Samir's list.
stories.elsewhere: A pass town with a genuinely bad scale comes off it.

stories.title: The Tree With a Debt
stories.holds: Hollis renews the pledge as guardianship instead of selling.
stories.elsewhere: The buyer has already bought other pledges along the road.

stories.title: Three Pots at Three Moon
stories.holds: One street shares its space; the newcomers get their permit.
stories.elsewhere: The smuggling rumors run on the next street over.
